text:
Alex: FYI CI is red on master for audit-validator tests — started ~09:22 BST. Failing asserts show customer PII left unredacted in golden fixtures.
Maria: ugh, which tests? link?
Alex: tests/integration/test_audit_golden.py::test_golden_redaction
Alex: failing output: ```
E       AssertionError: Found unredacted fields: ['user_email', 'ssn'] in /workspace/goldens/customer_events.json
E       AssertionError: 1 failed, 234 passed in 12.3s
```
Sam: hm I merged a small RBAC metadata PR last night that added `actor_metadata` with nested `contact` fields. Could be new keys bypassing the redactor whitelist.
Josh: Can you paste failing fixture snippet?
Alex: snippet: ```json
{
  "event_type": "access.grant",
  "actor": "service-account:ingest",
  "actor_metadata": { "contact": { "user_email": "alice@example.com" } },
  "resource": { "id": "acct_123", "owner_ssn": "123-45-6789" }
}
```
Maria: oh — `owner_ssn` ended up in resource.* instead of resource.metadata.* from the ingestion transform. That's customer-facing.
Vijay: CI log shows validator's redaction rule matches known top-level keys only. New nested paths from `actor_metadata.contact.user_email` won't be caught. Default behavior should be to redact any value matching PII patterns unless explicitly opted-out.
Sam: agreed. My PR added schema extension but didn't update the redactor. My bad.
Alex: repro locally: `pytest tests/integration/test_audit_golden.py::test_golden_redaction -q` and `python tools/audit_check.py --golden /workspace/goldens/customer_events.json --patterns patterns.yaml`
Josh: +1 to hotfix. Proposed immediate steps: 1) patch redactor to fallback to regex-based redaction for unknown fields, 2) add CI guard to fail on any email/ssn regex in goldens, 3) roll forward PR updating fixtures.
Maria: also need customer-impact assessment - did any logs get shipped unredacted to customers? Search S3 for uploads in last 24h. I'll ping ops. @ci-bot can you start a search job?
ci-bot: Job queued: s3-scan-9843. Results expected ~10m. Will post when done. :hourglass: 
audit-bot: diff summary: golden/customer_events.json +2 unredacted emails, +1 ssn. Patch to validator would have prevented this.
audit-bot: Suggested quick rule: treat any JSON leaf matching `\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b` or email regex as immediate redact unless path in `allowlist_fields` (config).
Vijay: Can we ship a tiny validator patch that treats unknown nested keys as sensitive by default? That reduces risk until we reconcile schema changes.
Sam: I'm drafting PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-validator/pull/462 — will include tests + CI guard.
Alex: If PR is ready in next 30m we can merge and cut a patch release. Ops, do we have an emergency deploy window?
Maria: SRE oncall pinged. They can expedite a hotfix deploy tonight. I'll coordinate on the runbook and customer comms if S3 scan shows exposures.
Josh: post-merge actions: backfill goldens, add a lint rule forbidding adding new top-level fields without corresponding redaction entry, and a short HOWTO for contributors.
Vijay: also add an automated schema-fuzzer that asserts redaction coverage for any newly added keys.
Sam: noted — I'll include a CI job that runs `tools/fuzz_redaction.py` against new PR diffs.
Alex: ok owners: Sam = fix PR and tests, Maria = ops/customer-impact, Vijay = redactor improvement, Josh = CI guard + docs. Can we have deploy + initial scan results by EOD?
ci-bot: s3-scan-9843 completed: 0 confirmed exposures to external buckets; 3 internal golden files with unredacted samples in CI artifacts only.
Maria: good => no customer-facing leak detected so far. Still high severity for CI hygiene.
Alex: thanks team. Follow-up meeting in 30m to confirm PR merge and deploy. Please add short notes to the incident thread. :thumbsup:
